_readme: Q89 inc.8 — the 2026-07-30 Martin Fierro Restaurant meeting (Naples, FL), as an Activity row the CRM can read.
WHY THIS ROW: inc.6 proved a write, inc.7 proved the write was a pipeline on a second company.
This is the third company through the SAME publisher, gate and surfaces with no new code — and
the first one where the read had to be EXECUTED first rather than taken from an earlier session.
It is the read log being drained, which is what inc.7 said inc.8 would be.
PROVENANCE — read before trusting a line of it. Every item below was read out of the Notion
Master Meetings Database page `Meeting 2026-07-30` (3ad1de57-0199-80dd-b213-d09c387217e7),
399 blocks / 89,170 chars, on 2026-08-05 via `find_meeting.py --page … --deep`, output archived
at `/tmp/q84-read-0730page.txt` (93,034 bytes) and logged in
`docs/research/Q84-READ-LOG-2026-08-05.md`. Nothing here was written from memory, from a summary
of a summary, or from another agent's prose.
FOUR FIELDS LIE ON THIS ROW TOO — Call Recording, Meeting Summary, Google Doc Link and Export
Status are all empty over 89k chars of body. That is now THREE rows out of three read (Omega
7/28, Gulf Coast 7/22, Martin Fierro 7/30). The recovery tool itself prints
'CONTRADICTED — the body below HAS the content. Trust the body, not the field.'
Field-emptiness is not evidence of absence anywhere in this system.
THE TITLE IS ALSO USELESS — `Meeting 2026-07-30` names no counterparty. The identity lives in
the PROPERTIES (`Company Meeting with: Martin Fierro Restaurant`, `Company URL`,
`Non MLE Attendees: Dani, Michael`), which is exactly the reason `find_meeting.py` prints
'TITLE (do not trust)'. The org was matched to the EXISTING prod record C-2005 by name; no new
org was created and none was guessed.
`sourceRef` addresses the LINE, not the meeting. `body ¶NNN` is the 1-based index of the block
among ALL `[paragraph]` blocks of the deep export in file order (342 of them; 336 non-empty) —
the same convention as the Omega and Gulf Coast files. `body to_do N` and
`body bullet «heading»` address the summary blocks. No `url` is set on any item ON PURPOSE: the
Notion page URL opens an 89k-char MEETING, not the sentence, and a link that lands the reader
somewhere other than where they were sent is the lie `intelSource.ts` refuses to tell.
PAIN POINTS ARE THE CLIENT'S OWN WORDS. Every pain `text` is a literal substring of its
`excerpt`, and every excerpt is a transcript paragraph spoken by the RESTAURANT side about their
own operation — not by Rob, not by Will, not by the AI summary. This transcript is a good one:
the owners talk about their own problems in plain sentences, so five pains are defensible where
Gulf Coast's messier recording yielded two. The count follows the evidence, never a target.
NOT WRITTEN, DELIBERATELY: the page's `Other Combined/Possible referral` field names SpotHopper,
Toast, Owner.com, Footy Coaches and 'Omega guys (Blake, Scott)'. Vendor tools named in passing
are not CRM orgs, and the Omega line is a REFERRAL thread that belongs to `company-catcher` and
Q87's gated-referral rules, not to this company's record. Writing them here would be the
'company invented from a tool mention' failure this queue already killed once.
NOT WRITTEN, DELIBERATELY (2): the '11 Proposed Automations' block and the claimed case-study
numbers ('50% consecutive monthly increases', 'guarantee a million views a month') are OUR pitch,
not their intel. A benefits-us item may make our commercial read; it may not launder our own
sales claims into the customer's record as findings.

intel.text: They repriced the menu three to four months ago toward value and volume — smaller shareable plates — deliberately trading margin for foot traffic. Every pitch has to be about heads through the door, not ticket size.
intel.excerpt: Recently repriced the menu toward a value/volume model — smaller, shareable plates at affordable price points to increase foot traffic

intel.text: Tourists are their stated priority target because they are less price-sensitive; Spanish-speaking guests are a second named segment. Argentine/Uruguayan cuisine plus Spanish-language content is the differentiator they already believe in.
intel.excerpt: Customer mix is broad: families, Spanish-speaking guests, Americans, and tourists; tourists are a priority target as they are less price-sensitive

intel.text: They already own the tools and know they are underusing them — Toast (POS), SpotHopper (email/SMS), a rewards program and a birthday club. The opening is integration and enablement, not another subscription.
intel.excerpt: Current tech stack includes Toast (POS), Spot Hopper (email/SMS marketing, acknowledged as underutilized), a rewards program, and a birthday club

intel.text: They track ticket average and know their guest count (~384/week off-season) — unusual for a restaurant this size, and the reason a lifetime-value / acquisition-cost conversation is available here when it is not elsewhere.
intel.excerpt: Currently averaging ~384 guests per week (off-season), with the bulk on Friday–Sunday

intel.text: On the website itself: no schema markup at all was the single most critical finding, and the meta description is more than double the 160-character limit so Google truncates it entirely. Both are checkable in front of them.
intel.excerpt: No schema markup — identified as the most critical missing element for SEO and AI engine visibility

intel.text: The Phase 1 deliverable list is already demoed, not promised — a new one-page AEO/SEO site with one-click call, WhatsApp and ordering was shown live on the call. The shortest path to signature is finishing that site with their real media rather than re-pitching the concept.
intel.excerpt: A new one-page site was demoed — AEO/SEO optimized, fast, and mobile-friendly

intel.text: The stated blocker is timing, not belief: the owners are interested and named off-season cash flow as the constraint, while agreeing off-season is the right time to build. A phased or deferred-start structure answers the actual objection.
intel.excerpt: Restaurant owners expressed interest but noted off-season cash flow as a constraint; acknowledged that off-season is the ideal time to implement

intel.text: Dani is the decision path — the owner says outright that Dani handles the technology, and the one action item that carries the deal is Dani working out how to move forward. Follow-ups go to Dani, not to the owner.
intel.excerpt: Believe it or not, I'm like the worst when it comes to technology. But Dani is the one that handles all of this.

intel.text: Being local is a live advantage here and was used on the call: the team can come in regularly to drive adoption, which is the direct answer to their own complaint that vendors never showed them how to use what they bought.
intel.excerpt: Tech team noted they are local and can come in regularly to help maximize system usage

intel.text: They run two locations and do catering, including a wedding booked into 2027 — the Phase 1 scope sold here is repeatable across the second location and a catering intake pipeline is already scoped for Phase 2.
